items.question: What is the R22 never-exceed airspeed (Vne) up to 3000 feet density altitude?
items.explanation: Section 2 AIRSPEED LIMITS gives Vne as 102 KIAS up to 3000 ft density altitude; above that, Vne is reduced per the placards on page 2-11.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: Above 3000 feet density altitude, how is R22 Vne determined?
options: It is reduced according to the cockpit placards
There is no Vne above 3000 ft
items.explanation: Above 3000 ft density altitude the POH refers the pilot to the Vne placards on page 2-11, which schedule a reduced Vne with increasing density altitude.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: What is the airspeed indicator green arc on the R22?
items.explanation: Section 2 INSTRUMENT MARKINGS lists the airspeed indicator green arc as 50 to 102 KIAS with the red line at 102 KIAS.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-8)

items.question: What is the power-on maximum rotor RPM limit?
items.explanation: Section 2 ROTOR SPEED LIMITS specifies power-on maximum 104% (530 RPM) and power-on minimum 101% (515 RPM).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the power-on minimum rotor RPM limit (standard tachometer)?
items.explanation: Power-on minimum is 101% (515 RPM). 97% (495 RPM) is permitted only on R22s with an O-320 engine and a tachometer with a 97% to 104% green arc.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the power-off maximum rotor RPM limit?
items.explanation: Section 2 ROTOR SPEED LIMITS gives power-off maximum 110% (561 RPM) and power-off minimum 90% (459 RPM).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the power-off minimum rotor RPM limit?
items.explanation: Power-off minimum rotor RPM is 90% (459 RPM).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: Transient rotor operation below the power-on minimum RPM is permitted only for what purpose?
items.explanation: A footnote to ROTOR SPEED LIMITS states transient operation at lower RPM is permitted for emergency-procedures training.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the maximum continuous engine speed for the R22?
items.explanation: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS list maximum continuous engine speed as 104% (2652 RPM); maximum transient is 106% (2700 RPM).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the maximum transient engine speed?
items.explanation: Maximum transient engine speed is 106% (2700 RPM). Intentional operation above the maximum continuous speed is prohibited.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the maximum cylinder head temperature (CHT)?
items.explanation: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS give a cylinder head maximum temperature of 500°F (260°C); the CHT gage green arc is 200 to 500°F.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS / INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-2, 2-9)

items.question: What is the maximum oil temperature?
items.explanation: Maximum oil temperature is 245°F (118°C); the oil temperature gage green arc is 75 to 245°F.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS / INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-2, 2-9)

items.question: What is the minimum oil pressure during flight?
items.explanation: Minimum oil pressure is 25 psi during idle and 55 psi during flight; maximum is 95 psi in flight and 115 psi during start and warm-up.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the maximum oil pressure during start and warm-up?
items.explanation: Maximum oil pressure during start and warm-up is 115 psi (vs 95 psi maximum during flight). The oil pressure gage upper red line is at 115 psi.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS / INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-2, 2-9)

items.question: What is the minimum oil quantity for takeoff?
items.explanation: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS specify a minimum oil quantity for takeoff of 4 qt (3.8 liters).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the carburetor air temperature (CAT) gage yellow arc?
items.explanation: The carburetor air temperature gage yellow arc is -15 to +5°C, the range in which carburetor icing is most likely.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-9)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight of the R22 Beta and Beta II?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight is 1370 lb (622 kg) for the Alpha, Beta and Beta II, and 1300 lb (590 kg) for the Standard and HP.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight of the R22 Standard and HP?
items.explanation: The Standard and HP have a maximum gross weight of 1300 lb (590 kg); the Alpha, Beta and Beta II are 1370 lb (622 kg).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the R22 minimum gross weight?
items.explanation: Minimum gross weight is 920 lb (417 kg).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum weight per seat, including that seat's baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum weight per seat, including the baggage compartment, is 240 lb (109 kg). Maximum in either baggage compartment alone is 50 lb (23 kg).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum weight allowed in either baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum in either baggage compartment is 50 lb (23 kg), subject also to the 240 lb combined seat-plus-compartment limit.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: Where is the R22 longitudinal reference datum located?
options: At the nose of the aircraft
100 inches forward of the main rotor shaft centerline
At the main rotor shaft centerline
items.explanation: The longitudinal reference datum is 100 inches forward of the main rotor shaft centerline.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITS (p.2-3); Sec 1 (p.1-7)

items.question: What is the R22 maximum operating density altitude?
items.explanation: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS give a maximum operating density altitude of 14,000 feet.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: Which maneuver is specifically prohibited because it can cause catastrophic loss of lateral control?
items.explanation: Low-G cyclic pushovers are prohibited: the resulting near-weightless condition can cause catastrophic loss of lateral control. Recover with immediate gentle aft cyclic.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: Under what circumstances may the R22 be flown with the governor selected off?
options: Any time at the pilot's discretion
Only for an in-flight system malfunction or emergency-procedures training
items.explanation: Flight is prohibited with the governor selected off, with exceptions only for an in-flight system malfunction or emergency-procedures training.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: Which systems must be operational for dispatch of the R22? (Select all that apply.)
items.explanation: The alternator, RPM governor, low rotor RPM warning system and OAT gage must all be operational for dispatch.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: What is the minimum flight crew, and from which seat is solo flight permitted?
options: One pilot in the right seat; solo from the right seat only
One pilot in the left seat; solo from the left seat only
items.explanation: Minimum crew is one pilot in the right seat; a flight instructor may act as PIC from the left seat, but solo flight is from the right seat only, and the left seat belt must be buckled.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: What personal equipment must each pilot wear during R22 operations?
items.explanation: A functioning headset must be worn by each pilot — on some aircraft the low RPM horn is provided only through the audio system.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: What does the R22 POH say about flight with the cabin doors removed?
options: Only the right door may be removed
Operation is approved with either or both doors removed, with loose items secured
A reduced Vne of 60 KIAS applies
items.explanation: Operation is approved with either or both cabin doors removed; loose items in the cabin must be properly secured during doors-off flight.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: For which kinds of operation is the R22 approved?
items.explanation: VFR day and night operations are approved. IFR operation is not approved; night VFR requires landing, navigation, instrument and anti-collision lights operational.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS (p.2-7)

items.question: What lighting must be operational for R22 night VFR operations?
options: Landing, navigation, instrument and anti-collision lights
items.explanation: VFR operation at night is permitted only when landing, navigation, instrument and anti-collision lights are operational.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the rotor tachometer lower red line?
items.explanation: The rotor tachometer lower red line is 90%, the upper red line is 110%, and the green arc is 101 to 104%.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-8)

items.question: What is the oil pressure gage green arc?
items.explanation: The oil pressure gage green arc is 55 to 95 psi (lower red line 25 psi, lower yellow 25–55, upper yellow 95–115, upper red 115). Earlier gages show a 60–90 psi green arc.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-9)

items.question: Under FAA Type Certificate H10WE, the R22 is approved as which category of rotorcraft?
items.explanation: The helicopter is approved as a normal-category rotorcraft under FAA Type Certificate No. H10WE (Models R22, R22 Alpha, R22 Beta and R22 Mariner).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: GENERAL (p.2-1)

items.question: Per FAA AD 95-26-04, flight is prohibited when surface winds (including gusts) exceed what value, unless the pilot meets the experience and SFAR 73 requirements?
items.explanation: AD 95-26-04 prohibits flight when surface winds exceed 25 knots including gusts, and when gust spreads exceed 15 knots, unless the pilot has 200+ helicopter hours (50 in the R22) plus SFAR 73 awareness training.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: INFORMATION PER FAA AD 95-26-04 (p.2-15)

items.question: Per FAA AD 95-26-04, on inadvertently encountering moderate or greater turbulence, forward airspeed should be adjusted to between 60 KIAS and 0.7 Vne, but no lower than what value?
items.explanation: AD 95-26-04 directs adjusting airspeed to between 60 KIAS and 0.7 Vne but no lower than 57 KIAS on an inadvertent turbulence encounter.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: INFORMATION PER FAA AD 95-26-04 (p.2-15)

items.question: With bladder-style tanks, what is the combined usable fuel quantity?
items.explanation: Bladder tanks: main 16.9 usable, auxiliary 9.4 usable, combined 26.3 US gal usable (28.0 total). Tanks without bladders give 29.7 usable but should no longer be in service per SB-109A.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FUEL LIMITATIONS (p.2-7)

items.question: Which statement about aerobatic flight in the R22 is correct?
items.explanation: Aerobatic flight is prohibited; abrupt control inputs may produce high fatigue stresses and cause catastrophic failure of a critical component.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: Which engine models are approved for the R22 series?
items.explanation: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS list one Lycoming Model O-320-A2B, -A2C, -B2C, or O-360-J2A (the O-360 in the Beta II is derated).
references: R22 POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2); Sec 1 DESCRIPTIVE DATA (p.1-5)

items.question: Is flight in known icing conditions permitted in the R22?
items.explanation: Flight in known icing conditions is prohibited.
references: R22 POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)
